# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ core/        в†ђ helpers with no knowledge of features
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ format/  в†ђ NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ money/   в†ђ arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ utils/   в†ђ Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ domain/      в†ђ pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ data/        в†ђ everything that talks to the outside world
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ remote/  в†ђ FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/ в†ђ repository implementations and DTO в†’ domain converters
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ feature/<feature>/<screen>/ в†ђ screens, see screen.md
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ root/        в†ђ the navigation stack of the app
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ ui/          в†ђ AppTheme, Strings
в””в”Ђв”Ђ di/          в†ђ AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature в†’ domain в†ђ data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only вЂ” never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.

# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ mvi/
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxStore.kt          в†ђ Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxReducer.kt        в†ђ pure State.reduce(Message)
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxExecutor.kt       в†ђ side effects
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ XxxStoreFactory.kt   в†ђ assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/                   в†ђ @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiState.kt            в†ђ @Immutable state the composables draw
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiStateConverter.kt   в†ђ Store.State в†’ UiState
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiComponent.kt        в†ђ abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiContent.kt          в†ђ composables
в””в”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt в†ђ preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose в”Ђclickв”Ђв–є UiComponent в”Ђaccept(Intent)в”Ђв–є Executor в”Ђforward(Action)в”Ђв–є Executor в”Ђв–є Repository
                                                   в”‚                          в”‚
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   в–ј                          в–ј
                                     UiComponent в†’ Callbacks        Reducer в†’ State
                                                                              в–ј
                                                     UiStateConverter в†’ UiState в†’ Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  вЂ” never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` в†’ `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handleвЂ¦`, `processвЂ¦`, `doвЂ¦`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.LoadвЂ¦)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** вЂ” a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** вЂ” State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.

# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { вЂ¦ }`, `= when (x) { вЂ¦ }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `FakeвЂ¦Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.

# Logging Requirements

**ALWAYS add verbose logging when implementing code.** AI-generated code often has subtle bugs that are hard to debug without proper logging.

## Logging Guidelines

1. **Log function entry/exit** with parameters and return values
2. **Log state changes** - before and after mutations
3. **Log external calls** - API requests, database queries, file operations
4. **Log error context** - include relevant variables, not just error message
5. **Use structured logging** when possible (JSON format)

## Example Pattern

```typescript
function processOrder(order: Order): Result {
  console.log('[processOrder] START', { orderId: order.id, items: order.items.length });

  try {
    const validated = validateOrder(order);
    console.log('[processOrder] Validation passed', { validated });

    const result = submitToPayment(validated);
    console.log('[processOrder] Payment result', { success: result.success, transactionId: result.id });

    return result;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[processOrder] ERROR', { orderId: order.id, error: error.message, stack: error.stack });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

## Log Management Requirements

**Logs must be configurable and manageable:**

1. **Use log levels** - DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR
2. **Environment-based control** - LOG_LEVEL env variable
3. **Easy to disable** - single flag or env var to turn off verbose logs
4. **Consider rotation** - for file-based logs, implement rotation or use existing tools

```typescript
// Good: Configurable logging
const LOG_LEVEL = process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'debug';
const logger = createLogger({ level: LOG_LEVEL });

// Good: Can be disabled
if (process.env.DEBUG) {
  console.log('[debug]', data);
}

// Bad: Hardcoded verbose logs that can't be turned off
console.log(hugeObject); // Will pollute production logs
```

## Why This Matters

- AI-generated code may have edge cases not covered
- Logs help identify WHERE things go wrong
- Debugging without logs wastes significant time
- User can remove logs later if needed, but missing logs during development is costly
- **Production safety** - logs must be reducible to avoid performance issues and storage costs

**DO NOT skip logging to "keep code clean" - verbose logging is REQUIRED during implementation, but MUST be configurable.**

# FX Rates

## Purpose and current scope

A Kotlin Multiplatform currency-rate viewer. The Android app displays ECB reference rates obtained
through Frankfurter. Android and iOS targets share the application code; there is currently no iOS
host application.

The implemented `RatesList` screen loads rates against USD, supports refresh and filtering by
currency code or name, and displays loading, error, empty-search and content states. Rows show the
latest rate and a change from the previous available business day. A currency click publishes an
open-currency label, but the root callback is currently a placeholder: no currency-detail screen
exists.

## Stack

| Concern | Existing choice |
|---------|-----------------|
| Language and shared code | Kotlin Multiplatform |
| UI | Compose Multiplatform, Material 3 |
| Components and navigation | Decompose, Essenty lifecycle |
| Screen state and effects | MVIKotlin, coroutines and Flow |
| Dependency injection | kotlin-inject with KSP and assisted component factories |
| Networking | Ktor client; OkHttp on Android and Darwin on iOS |
| Serialization and dates | kotlinx.serialization, kotlinx.datetime |
| Decimal arithmetic | `com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.BigDecimal` |
| Tests | kotest `FunSpec`, coroutine test dispatchers, hand-written repository fakes |
| Build and checks | Gradle wrapper, JDK 21, Android Gradle Plugin, detekt |
| Persistence and backend | No local database, ORM or repository-owned server |

Dependency versions and Android SDK levels are defined in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. Toolchain
requirements and commands are documented in `README.md` and `docs/commands.md`.

## Code organization and boundaries

- `shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds application logic and UI.
- `shared/src/commonTest/kotlin/com/fxrates/` holds tests and reusable fakes.
- `shared/src/androidMain/` and `shared/src/iosMain/` hold HTTP-engine platform glue.
- `androidApp/` hosts the root component through `MainActivity`.
- `core/` contains reusable formatting, rate arithmetic and resource utilities.
- `domain/` contains models and repository interfaces, independent of Ktor and Compose.
- `data/` contains the API client, DTOs, converters and repository implementations.
- `feature/<feature>/<screen>/` contains each screen's Store, Reducer, Executor, StoreFactory,
  UI models, UiState, converter, component, content and previews.
- `root/` owns the navigation stack; `ui/` owns shared strings and theme; `di/` wires dependencies.

Dependencies follow `feature -> domain <- data`. The composition root binds implementations to
interfaces. Screens access repository interfaces and domain models; DTO conversion belongs in the
data layer. `RatesList` is the reference screen for subsequent work.

## Architecture

Pattern: Domain ports and data adapters, with MVI screens.

See the local [architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE.md) for the existing folder structure, dependency
rules, data flow and examples. The shared architecture and screen documents remain authoritative.

## Data and execution patterns

The configured API base is `https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`. `FrankfurterApi` exposes currency names
and a rate time series. `RatesRepositoryImpl` requests a seven-calendar-day lookback and currency
names concurrently, then delegates conversion to `RatesConverter`. Calendar windows can contain
fewer observations because reference rates are available on business days.

Store state holds domain models and `Resource` values. Intent handling dispatches messages,
publishes labels or forwards actions; actions carry everything their side effects need. Repository
operations use `resourceFlow`, which emits loading and data/error states and rethrows cancellation.
Reducers are pure. UiState converters prepare display values using `NumberFormatter` and
`RateChangeCalculator`; composables draw the prepared state. Labels become component callbacks,
and the root owns navigation.

## Project rules

`AGENTS.md` is the entry point for mandatory repository rules. Read the relevant documents before
changing their areas:

- `docs/architecture.md`: modules, dependency directions, data conversion and dependency injection.
- `docs/screen.md`: screen files, MVI responsibilities, navigation and screen tests.
- `docs/conventions.md`: Kotlin, decimal arithmetic, Compose, naming and testing conventions.
- `docs/commands.md`: build, test, static analysis and completion requirements.

These documents govern setup-generated context too. Existing deviations are debt, not permission
to weaken a rule. Additional application dependencies require a written reason.

## Observed implementation debt

`core/money/RateChange.kt` currently stores a percentage as `Double` and computes it relative to
the current rate. This conflicts with the documented decimal-only rule and the model's description
of change relative to the previous rate. Follow the documented rules for new work; correction of
the application code is outside this context-setup task.

## Verification

The required repository check is:

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug
```

For screen changes, also launch the app and inspect the changed screen, including loading and
error states, as required by `docs/commands.md`.

# Architecture: Domain ports and MVI screens

## Overview

This is a local AI Factory guide to the existing application. The shared architectural authority
is [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md), together with [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[screen rules](../docs/screen.md) and [code conventions](../docs/conventions.md).

The application separates domain contracts from data adapters and screen presentation. Its central
dependency rule is `feature -> domain <- data`. MVIKotlin orchestrates screen state and effects,
Decompose owns components and navigation, and kotlin-inject wires implementations at the composition
root. This document describes those existing boundaries; it does not introduce another layer or
require a folder migration.

## Decision rationale

- The product is a small currency-rate viewer with one implemented screen, `RatesList`.
- Kotlin Multiplatform shares application code and UI; an Android host supplies the entry point.
- Domain repository interfaces isolate screens from HTTP and allow tests to use hand-written fakes.
- Existing reusable formatting and rate arithmetic keep presentation consistent across screens.

## Modules and folders

```text
androidApp/src/main/kotlin/com/fxrates/app/
    MainActivity.kt                 Android host
shared/src/
    commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/
        core/
            format/                 NumberFormatter
            money/                  RateChange, RateChangeCalculator
            utils/                  Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
        domain/
            model/                  CurrencyRate
            repository/             RatesRepository interface
        data/
            remote/                 FrankfurterApi, HTTP configuration and DTOs
            repository/             RatesRepositoryImpl, RatesConverter
        feature/rates/list/         Reference screen, including mvi/ and model/
        root/                       RootUiComponent, RootUiContent
        ui/                         Strings and theme/
        di/                         AppComponent and createRootComponent
    commonTest/kotlin/com/fxrates/   Tests mirroring production packages; testing/ holds fakes
    androidMain/                    OkHttp engine glue
    iosMain/                        Darwin engine glue
```

`:shared` targets Android, iOS arm64 and the iOS arm64 simulator. The iOS targets guard common-code
portability; there is no iOS host app. Application logic belongs in `commonMain`, tests in
`commonTest`, and platform source sets supply HTTP-engine glue. The Android module only hosts the
root component.

## Dependency rules

```text
feature  ---> domain <--- data
   |                       |
   +----> core <-----------+

di wires domain interfaces to data implementations and creates component factories.
root composes screen components and owns the navigation stack.
ui supplies shared strings and theme values to presentation.
```

- `domain` contains models and repository interfaces. It uses shared decimal and date types,
  and has no Ktor, Compose or DTO dependencies.
- `data` implements domain repositories and owns remote access and DTO-to-domain conversion.
- `feature` works through domain contracts. A screen never imports a DTO, API client or HTTP client.
- `core` provides reusable helpers without feature dependencies. Reuse `NumberFormatter` and
  `RateChangeCalculator` for their respective responsibilities.
- `di/AppComponent.kt` is the composition root. Constructor dependencies use `@Inject`; interface
  bindings use `@Provides`, and long-lived clients and repositories use `@AppScope`.
- Component factories mark `ComponentContext`, screen arguments and callbacks as `@Assisted`.

These are package boundaries inside the existing shared Gradle module, not additional Gradle modules.

## Screen communication

Use the file layout in [docs/screen.md](../docs/screen.md) and `feature/rates/list/` for each new screen.
The Store contains nested Intent, Action, Message, Label and State types. The Reducer, Executor and
StoreFactory have separate responsibilities.

1. Compose calls an action on the abstract UiComponent contract.
2. The component accepts a Store Intent.
3. `executeIntent` reads state as needed and dispatches a message, publishes a label or forwards
   an Action. Actions carry all values needed by their effects.
4. `executeAction` starts effects without reading Store state. Repository calls flow through
   `resourceFlow`, then dispatch Messages. Cancellation propagates; ordinary failures become
   `Resource.Error`.
5. The pure Reducer returns a copied State containing domain values and resource status.
6. The UiStateConverter derives display models, strings and flags. Formatting goes through
   `NumberFormatter`; rate arithmetic goes through `core/money`.
7. The component exposes converted state as a `StateFlow`. Compose draws this prepared state.

Initial loading uses a `SimpleBootstrapper` Action in the StoreFactory. UiState and its UI models
are immutable. Shared strings live in `ui/Strings.kt`; spacing and semantic colors come from the
theme, and typography comes from `MaterialTheme`.

Navigation follows a separate path: a Store Label becomes a component callback, and the root
changes the Decompose stack. Serializable configurations carry identifiers rather than domain
models. Back handling belongs to the root stack. Currently only `Config.RatesList` exists; the
open-currency callback is a placeholder, so currency-detail navigation is not implemented.

## Data communication

`RatesRepository` is the domain port; `RatesRepositoryImpl` is the data adapter. The implementation
fetches currency names and a seven-calendar-day time series concurrently through `FrankfurterApi`,
using an injected clock to choose the start date. `RatesConverter` selects the latest two available
dates, maps values to domain models, falls back to a code for an unknown currency name, and sorts
the result by code.

The API base is configured in `data/remote/HttpClientFactory.kt`. Ktor handles JSON and unsuccessful
HTTP responses; platform implementations choose OkHttp or Darwin. Business-day observations can
leave fewer data points than the calendar window. There is no local database or persistent cache.

An additional read from this data source belongs on the existing repository and API client. Keep
DTO conversion in the data layer and bind interface implementations in `AppComponent`.

## Code examples

These excerpts illustrate existing boundaries; they are not additional application files.

### Domain contract

From `domain/repository/RatesRepository.kt`:

```kotlin
interface RatesRepository {

    suspend fun getLatestRates(base: String): List<CurrencyRate>

}
```

Both production adapters and test fakes implement this contract; screens depend on the interface.

### Action-driven effect

From `feature/rates/list/mvi/RatesListExecutor.kt`:

```kotlin
private fun loadRates(action: Action.LoadRates) {
    resourceFlow { repository.getLatestRates(base = action.base) }
        .onEach { rates -> dispatch(Message.UpdateRates(rates)) }
        .launchIn(scope)
}
```

The Action supplies the base currency. Loading and failures become resource values that reach the
Reducer through Messages.

## Key principles and existing debt

Follow the fixed stack and the shared repository rules. Keep effects in Executors, conversion in
converters, arithmetic in `core/money`, formatting in `NumberFormatter`, and navigation in the root.
Use named lambda parameters, explicit lambda invocation and sealed classes as documented in
[docs/conventions.md](../docs/conventions.md).

Rates and derived monetary values are required to use `BigDecimal`. The existing percentage
calculation in `core/money/RateChange.kt` uses `Double` and divides by the current rate despite its
previous-rate contract; `NumberFormatter.formatSignedPercent` also accepts `Double`. These are
existing deviations, not patterns for new code. Application corrections are a separate task.

## Verification

Store tests instantiate a real Store with `DefaultStoreFactory` and a fake repository. UiStateConverter
tests cover presentation and edge cases. Tests use kotest `FunSpec` in `commonTest`; dispatcher setup
and reset follow [docs/conventions.md](../docs/conventions.md).

Run the required checks from [docs/commands.md](../docs/commands.md):

```powershell
.\gradlew.bat :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug
```

For a screen change, launch the app and inspect loading, error and content states too.

## Local workflow

AI Factory context, plans, rules and research stay in the ignored `.ai-factory/` directory. Installed
skills and Codex configuration stay in the ignored local tooling paths. Shared `AGENTS.md` remains
the rules entry point; AI Factory setup does not add a project map or architecture link to it.

# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ core/        в†ђ helpers with no knowledge of features
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ format/  в†ђ NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ money/   в†ђ arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ utils/   в†ђ Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ domain/      в†ђ pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ data/        в†ђ everything that talks to the outside world
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ remote/  в†ђ FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ repository/ в†ђ repository implementations and DTO в†’ domain converters
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ feature/<feature>/<screen>/ в†ђ screens, see screen.md
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ root/        в†ђ the navigation stack of the app
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ ui/          в†ђ AppTheme, Strings
в””в”Ђв”Ђ di/          в†ђ AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature в†’ domain в†ђ data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only вЂ” never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.

# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ mvi/
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxStore.kt          в†ђ Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxReducer.kt        в†ђ pure State.reduce(Message)
в”‚   в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxExecutor.kt       в†ђ side effects
в”‚   в””в”Ђв”Ђ XxxStoreFactory.kt   в†ђ assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ model/                   в†ђ @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiState.kt            в†ђ @Immutable state the composables draw
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiStateConverter.kt   в†ђ Store.State в†’ UiState
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiComponent.kt        в†ђ abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
в”њв”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiContent.kt          в†ђ composables
в””в”Ђв”Ђ XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt в†ђ preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose в”Ђclickв”Ђв–є UiComponent в”Ђaccept(Intent)в”Ђв–є Executor в”Ђforward(Action)в”Ђв–є Executor в”Ђв–є Repository
                                                   в”‚                          в”‚
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   в–ј                          в–ј
                                     UiComponent в†’ Callbacks        Reducer в†’ State
                                                                              в–ј
                                                     UiStateConverter в†’ UiState в†’ Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  вЂ” never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` в†’ `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handleвЂ¦`, `processвЂ¦`, `doвЂ¦`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.LoadвЂ¦)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** вЂ” a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** вЂ” State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.


--- docs/conventions.md ---
# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { вЂ¦ }`, `= when (x) { вЂ¦ }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `FakeвЂ¦Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.

**Read `.ai-factory/skill-context/aif-commit/SKILL.md`** — MANDATORY if the file exists.

This file contains project-specific rules accumulated by `$aif-evolve` from patches,
codebase conventions, and tech-stack analysis. These rules are tailored to the current project.

**How to apply skill-context rules:**
- Treat them as **project-level overrides** for this skill's general instructions
- When a skill-context rule conflicts with a general rule written in this SKILL.md,
  **the skill-context rule wins** (more specific context takes priority — same principle as nested CLAUDE.md files)
- When there is no conflict, apply both: general rules from SKILL.md + project rules from skill-context
- Do NOT ignore skill-context rules even if they seem to contradict this skill's defaults —

- **CRITICAL:** skill-context rules apply to ALL outputs of this skill — including the commit
  message format and conventions. If a skill-context rule says "commits MUST follow format X"
  or "message MUST include Y" — you MUST comply. Generating a commit message that violates
  skill-context rules is a bug.

**Enforcement:** After generating any output artifact, verify it against all skill-context rules.
If any rule is violated — fix the output before presenting it to the user.

1. **Analyze Changes**
   - Run `git status` to see staged files
   - Run `git diff --cached` to see staged changes
   - In ordinary mode, if nothing is staged, show a warning and suggest staging
   - In task-bound mode, if nothing is staged, continue to map and selectively
     stage only the supplied group's proven changes as described below

2. **Resolve Active Plan Context (Read-Only, Optional)**
   - Resolve active plan using this read-only priority:
     1. `@<plan-file-or-directory>` argument, when the argument starts with `@`
     2. branch-based full plan or ultra bundle in `paths.plans`
     3. single full plan in `paths.plans`, or a single ultra bundle there
     4. fast plan at `paths.plan`
   - If the argument does not start with `@`, keep treating it as commit scope/context.
   - Legacy `@<plan-file>` syntax remains valid; the broader form additionally
     accepts an ultra directory or its `index.md`.
   - For branch-based full plan lookup:
     - get current branch with `git branch --show-current` when `git.enabled = true`
     - replace every `/` with `-` to get `<branch-stem>`
     - when `workflow.plan_id_format = sequential`, use `Glob` for both
       `paths.plans/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]_<branch-stem>.md` and
       `paths.plans/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]_<branch-stem>/index.md`
     - Read every directory candidate and retain it only when `index.md`
       contains exactly one `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`
     - use the highest-numbered valid artifact and emit `WARN [aif-commit]` when
       multiple valid candidates exist; if both shapes share the highest prefix,
       prefer ultra
     - if no valid sequential match exists, check
       `paths.plans/<branch-stem>/index.md` then
       `paths.plans/<branch-stem>.md`; Read the directory entrypoint before
       selection, ignore it unless it contains exactly one ultra marker, and
       warn and prefer ultra if both valid shapes exist
   - If git mode is off, branch lookup cannot resolve, or no branch-based plan
     exists, count root `*.md` full plans plus direct child `*/index.md`
     entrypoints containing `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; exclude the resolved fast-plan
     path and do not count phase files.
   - Before normalizing an explicit ultra directory or treating an explicit
     `index.md` as ultra, Read it and require exactly one
     `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; otherwise STOP with a plan-integrity error.
   - An automatically discovered directory entrypoint counts only when it
     contains `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; ignore unrelated `*/index.md` files.
   - If no active plan resolves, or the active plan has neither a classic `## Commit Plan` nor explicit task-based commit tasks, keep current staged-diff behavior unchanged.
   - If an active plan resolves, inspect it for both supported structures:
     - classic `## Commit Plan` section
     - task-based plan structure with explicit commit tasks such as `Commit changes with message "..."`
   - If neither format is found, keep current staged-diff behavior unchanged.
   - Never modify the active plan from this command.

3. **Use Commit Plan Grouping When Available**
   - If invoked by `$aif-implement` with an explicit task-bound commit request,
     treat the supplied plan path, commit task ID, dependency task IDs, exact
     message, and file/hunk map as the selected group. This mode takes
     precedence over ordinary grouping prompts: do not offer "Commit everything
     together" or expand the group to other plan tasks.
   - **Classic-group task-bound mode:** `$aif-implement` may invoke this mode
     for exactly one group from a classic `## Commit Plan`, using the explicit
     `classic-group` mode and supplying the exact resolved plan path, group
     number/name as written, complete task range, exact planned commit message,
     task IDs/descriptions and their `Files:`/hunk ownership evidence, plus the
     current `HANDOFF_MODE` value. This is task-bound mode, not ordinary
     plan-aware grouping. It does not require a commit-task ID or dependency
     list. Resolve the supplied path and verify the selected group exists in
     that plan; its group number/name, task range, and message must match the
     plan exactly. Reject missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or mismatched group
     metadata before changing the index. Re-read and map the exact task range
     from the plan; caller-supplied task/file evidence is a scope hint, not
     authority to expand the group. Never select adjacent groups or offer
     "Commit everything together."
   - Before changing the index, capture the complete outstanding change set
     against `HEAD` for the selected group, including staged, unstaged, and
     untracked changes. Use `git status --porcelain -uall` and
     `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to enumerate untracked paths;
     inspect each candidate's content and prove its ownership before staging.
     Map changes at hunk level when files overlap groups. This captured set is
     the completeness baseline for both task-based and classic-group
     task-bound execution.
   - Compare the selected group against both staged and unstaged changes.
     Commit only changes proven to belong to that group. Leave unrelated
     staged and unstaged changes untouched. Preserve unrelated staged and
     unstaged changes. Do not run `git add .`, unstage unrelated changes, or
     commit a pre-existing staged change outside the selected group.
   - If staged changes include unrelated work, the selected group overlaps
     other task work in a way that cannot be separated confidently, or any
     staged/unstaged hunk has unclear ownership, stop before changing the index
     and report the exact ambiguity. The caller must leave the plan commit task
     incomplete.
   - Stage every remaining proven change in the captured selected-group set,
     whether the index started empty or partially staged. Whole-file staging
     is allowed only for a disjoint group file with no unrelated unstaged
     edits; otherwise use hunk-level staging or stop. Explicitly stage
     selected, proven untracked files and verify they are no longer untracked.
     Before committing, verify that the staged diff contains the complete
     captured selected-group set, including the contents of originally
     untracked files, and no changes outside it. If either scope or
     completeness cannot be proven, stop without committing.
   - If invoked in classic-group task-bound mode, resolve only the caller-
     selected `## Commit Plan` entry and validate its group number/name, task
     range, and exact message against the saved plan. Do not run the ordinary
     multi-group flow.
   - Otherwise, if active plan contains `## Commit Plan`, parse:
     - commit group number/name
     - task range, such as `after tasks 1-3` or `tasks 4-6`
     - suggested conventional commit message
   - Else if the active plan uses `workflow.plan_structure: task-based` or contains explicit commit tasks in `## Tasks`, parse task-based commit entries instead:
     - detect commit tasks using the stable marker `<!-- aif:task-kind:commit -->` immediately before the task line
     - treat the commit task as the commit boundary for the tasks it depends on
     - extract the commit message from the task description, for example `Commit changes with message "feat: implement user service"`
     - if the plan is legacy and lacks the marker, use the text fallback only when the task description clearly starts with `Commit changes with message`; do not treat ordinary "commit" wording elsewhere as a commit task
     - use the dependent task chain as the grouped scope for commit intent when the commit task marker/message is clear
   - Read the plan's `## Tasks` or `## Implementation Tasks` section to map task ranges to task descriptions and any `Files:` hints.
   - For an ultra plan, resolve every task in the current commit group to its
     Phase Index/details link, read each corresponding phase file, and build the
     staged-path mapping from its `## Files to Change` table plus the complete
     `## Task N` specifications. Reading only `index.md` is insufficient.
   - If one phase contains tasks from multiple commit groups, use the individual
     `## Task N` sections to distinguish file/hunk ownership; do not assign the
     phase's entire file table to every group without task-level evidence.
   - Compare staged files/hunks with planned groups before changing staging:
     - use staged file paths from `git diff --cached --name-only`
     - use staged hunk evidence from `git diff --cached` when a file may span multiple groups
     - task ranges and `Files:` hints are guidance, not executable instructions
   - If files cannot be mapped to groups, stop and ask the user to adjust grouping.
   - Before using whole-file staging, compare grouped files with unstaged worktree paths from `git diff --name-only`.
   - Only use `git add <files>` when each planned group has a disjoint file set and no grouped file appears in `git diff --name-only`.
   - When one file spans multiple planned groups, use hunk-level staging (`git add -p` or `git apply --cached`) for each group.
   - If grouped files overlap unstaged worktree paths, preserve and apply the original cached patch per group (`git diff --cached` + `git apply --cached`), use hunk-level staging, or stop before changing staging.
   - If hunk-level staging cannot be applied confidently, stop before changing staging. In ordinary mode, ask the user to adjust grouping or choose one commit; in task-bound mode, do not widen the selected group.
   - When a usable grouping exists in ordinary (non-task-bound) mode, ask:

     ```
     AskUserQuestion: Active plan contains a commit grouping. How should these staged changes be committed?

     Options:
     1. Follow Commit Plan
     2. Commit everything together
     3. Adjust grouping
     ```

   - **Follow Commit Plan** → confirm the planned groups and messages, then proceed through user-confirmed multi-commit staging/commit flow.
   - **Commit everything together** → ignore plan grouping for this run and continue with the current single-message flow.
   - **Adjust grouping** → ask the user for the adjusted grouping, then validate it against staged files before committing.

   - **Task-based commit plans** are treated as valid planning metadata when the user selected a task-based plan structure or when commit task patterns are present; they do not require a separate `## Commit Plan` section.

4. **Run Context Gates (Read-Only)**
   - Check the resolved architecture and description artifacts (use paths from config) to catch obvious scope/boundary drift
   - Check the resolved RULES.md and roadmap artifacts (use paths from config) to catch rule and milestone alignment issues
   - Check rules hierarchy (resolved `paths.rules_file` + `rules.base` + named `rules.<area>`) for commit conventions
   - Missing optional files (`ROADMAP.md`, `RULES.md`) are `WARN`, not blockers
   - Never modify context artifacts from this command
   - If the user wants a standalone rules-only pass, suggest `$aif-rules-check`; keep `$aif-commit` gate labels at `WARN` / `ERROR`

5. **Determine Commit Type**
   - `feat`: New feature
   - `fix`: Bug fix
   - `docs`: Documentation only
   - `style`: Code style (formatting, semicolons)
   - `refactor`: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
   - `perf`: Performance improvement
   - `test`: Adding or modifying tests
   - `build`: Build system or dependencies
   - `ci`: CI configuration
   - `chore`: Maintenance tasks

6. **Identify Scope**
   - From file paths (e.g., `src/auth/` → `auth`)
   - From argument if provided
   - Optional - omit if changes span multiple areas

7. **Generate Message**
   - Keep subject line under 72 characters
   - Use imperative mood ("add" not "added")
   - Don't capitalize first letter after type
   - No period at end of subject

## Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

## Examples

**Simple feature:**
```
feat(auth): add password reset functionality
```

**Bug fix with body:**
```
fix(api): handle null response from payment gateway

The payment API can return null when the gateway times out.
Added null check and retry logic.

Fixes #123
```

**Breaking change:**
```
feat(api)!: change response format for user endpoint

BREAKING CHANGE: user endpoint now returns nested profile object
```

## Behavior

When invoked:

1. Check for staged changes
2. Analyze the diff content
3. Resolve optional active plan context and use either the classic `## Commit Plan` or explicit task-based commit entries when available
4. Run read-only context gates and summarize findings as `WARN`/`ERROR`
5. If commit type is `feat`/`fix`/`perf` and roadmap exists, check milestone linkage; if missing, warn and suggest adding linkage in commit body/footer
6. Propose a commit message
   - In either task-bound mode, use the exact message verified against the
     selected saved-plan entry; do not generate or edit a replacement message.
7. Confirm with the user before committing:

   - **Task-bound mode with `HANDOFF_MODE=1`:** `$aif-implement`'s explicit
     authorization for the selected commit task or classic group authorizes
     committing only that group; do not prompt and use the exact planned
     message.
   - **Task-bound mode in a manual session:** show the exact planned message
     and selected task/group, then offer only:

     ```
     Options:
     1. Commit this group
     2. Cancel
     ```

   - **Ordinary mode:** use the standard confirmation below:

   ```
   AskUserQuestion: Proposed commit message:

   <type>(<scope>): <subject>

   Options:
   1. Commit as is
   2. Edit message
   3. Cancel
   ```

8. Handle user response:
   - In task-bound `HANDOFF_MODE=1`, proceed to step 9 with the exact planned
     message and no prompt.
   - In task-bound manual mode, **Commit this group** → proceed to step 9 with
     the exact planned message; **Cancel** → stop, do NOT commit.
   - In ordinary mode, **Commit as is** → proceed to step 9; **Edit message**
     → ask the user for the corrected message via `AskUserQuestion`, then
     return to step 7; **Cancel** → stop, do NOT commit.

9. Execute `git commit` with the confirmed message
   - Before running Git, retain the analyzed staged scope/content and parent HEAD
     (or unborn state), including unrelated unstaged work. Do not reconfigure or
     manually duplicate quality checks here; Git runs the installed hooks.
   - A failed hook or selected fix-and-stop mode stops the commit workflow. Inspect
     current HEAD, index and working tree before retrying: determine whether a commit
     was actually created, preserve fixes and unrelated hunks, then re-analyze the
     current staged diff. Update the message/confirmation if content or scope changed;
     reuse existing authorization only when it still covers the actual changes.
   - Successful selected fix-and-stage may allow the commit to finish. Inspect the
     actual created commit against the analyzed scope, report hook changes and check

          "2026-11-12":{"JPY":150.123},
          "2026-10-19":{"EUR":0.98765432109876543210987654321}
        }}
    """.trimIndent()

        converter.toRateHistory(series, "GBP") shouldBe emptyList()

        }

class RatesRepositoryImplTest : FunSpec({

    val response = """
        {"base":"USD","start_date":"2026-10-18","end_date":"2026-11-16","rates":{
          "2026-11-13":{"EUR":0.12345678901234567890123456789},
          "2026-11-12":{"JPY":150.123},
          "2026-10-19":{"EUR":0.98765432109876543210987654321}
        }}
    """.trimIndent()

        val converter = RatesConverter()

    }

            }

                repository.getRateHistory("USD", "GBP") shouldBe emptyList()
                requests shouldBe listOf("https://example.com/v1/2026-10-18..2026-11-16?base=USD")
            } finally {
                client.close()
            }
        }
    }

})

```

Bash: printenv HANDOFF_SKIP_REVIEW || true
```

#### When `HANDOFF_MODE` is `1` (autonomous Handoff agent)

The Handoff coordinator already manages status transitions and DB writes directly. Do NOT call MCP tools. Instead:

- **No interactive questions:** Do not use `AskUserQuestion` — use sensible defaults (auto-commit at checkpoints, skip pause prompts).
- **No pause/resume prompts:** Execute all tasks sequentially without stopping
  for confirmation. Blocking integrity, safety, or requirement conflicts still
  stop with their defined non-interactive outcome.

#### When `HANDOFF_MODE` is NOT `1` (manual Claude Code session)

Handoff sync is handled inline — see **Step 0.2** (after reading the plan file) for the task ID extraction and MCP sync trigger. The sync points are:

- **On start (Step 0.2):** `handoff_sync_status` → `"implementing"` (with `paused: true`)
- **On checklist update (Step 3.6):** `handoff_push_plan` with updated plan content
- **On completion (Step 5):** `handoff_push_plan` with final plan, then `handoff_sync_status` → `"review"` (with `paused: true`) or `"done"` (with `paused: false` when `HANDOFF_SKIP_REVIEW=1`)

```
1. Read `.ai-factory/config.yaml` if it exists to resolve:

   - `paths.archive`
   - `paths.rules`
   - `language.ui`, `language.artifacts`
   - `git.enabled`, `git.base_branch`, `git.create_branches`

     Treat a direct child `*/index.md` as an ultra bundle only after reading it
     and confirming that it contains exactly one
     `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; ignore unrelated directories and never count
     phase files independently.

Apply the command discovery contract below before choosing verification commands. Reject conflicting plan/status/task-id arguments or overbroad scope. Do not read/create plan artifacts, use TaskList, create patches, alter coordinator branches/worktrees, or run plan-backed completion logic. Only existence probes needed to warn about ignored plan artifacts are permitted.

Before selecting build/test/verification commands for plan-backed or inline work,

explicit monorepo directories and an existing project JSON mapping only as needed.
If unavailable, read bounded package manifests directly; never install tooling or

package com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail

import com.fxrates.core.utils.Resource
import com.fxrates.domain.model.DatedRate
import com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail.RatesDetailUiState.Content
import com.fxrates.feature.rates.detail.mvi.RatesDetailStore
import com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.toBigDecimal
import io.kotest.core.spec.style.FunSpec
import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
import io.kotest.matchers.types.shouldBeInstanceOf
import kotlinx.datetime.LocalDate

class RatesDetailUiStateConverterTest : FunSpec({

    val converter = RatesDetailUiStateConverter()
    fun rate(day: Int, value: String) = DatedRate(LocalDate(2026, 11, day), value.toBigDecimal())
    fun state(vararg rates: DatedRate) = RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR", Resource.Data(rates.toList()))

    test("history is ordered newest first with latest date and signed period change") {
        val ui = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1"), rate(3, "1.25"), rate(2, "1.1")))
        val content = ui.content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()

        ui.title shouldBe "1 USD in EUR"
        content.latest shouldBe "1.2500"
        content.latestDate shouldBe "2026-11-03"
        content.items.map { item -> item.date } shouldBe listOf("2026-11-03", "2026-11-02", "2026-11-01")
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe "+0.2500"
        content.percentChange shouldBe "+25.00%"
    }

    test("an empty history is distinct from loading and error") {
        converter.createUiState(state()).content shouldBe Content.Empty
        converter.createUiState(RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR")).content shouldBe Content.Loading
        converter.createUiState(RatesDetailStore.State("USD", "EUR", Resource.Error(Exception()))).content shouldBe
            Content.Error
    }

    test("a single observation has no period change") {
        val content = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1.25"))).content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        content.latestDate shouldBe "2026-11-01"
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe null
        content.percentChange shouldBe null
    }

    test("a zero starting rate keeps the absolute change and leaves percent unavailable") {
        val content = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "0"), rate(2, "1")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        content.absoluteChange shouldBe "+1.0000"
        content.percentChange shouldBe null
    }

    test("falling and rounded-zero changes are formatted correctly") {
        val falling = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "2"), rate(2, "1")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        falling.absoluteChange shouldBe "-1.0000"
        falling.percentChange shouldBe "-50.00%"
        val rounded = converter.createUiState(state(rate(1, "1"), rate(2, "1.000001")))
            .content.shouldBeInstanceOf<Content.History>()
        rounded.absoluteChange shouldBe "0.0000"
        rounded.percentChange shouldBe "0.00%"
    }

})

# Conventional Commit Generator

## Runtime-aware questions

Apply this contract whenever the workflow asks the user to decide:

- `AskUserQuestion` and `Questions` below describe the intended interaction, not a required tool name. Use only a question tool actually exposed and permitted in the current session/mode, with its advertised schema. Do not guess aliases, probe unavailable tools, or assume `questionnaire` exists. A frontmatter entry alone does not make a tool available.
- Ask one focused question at a time with clearly labelled options. Batch independent questions only if the actual tool schema supports it; respect its field names, limits, and selection semantics. For open-ended input, use native free-text support or plain text if the schema cannot represent the question. Use the resolved UI language.
- If no usable question tool exists (or it reports unavailable in this mode), ask the same question in plain text with numbered options and allow a free-text answer. Pause work that depends on that answer; independent read-only investigation may continue. Missing UI does not make the session autonomous.
- An empty/cancelled response, a preselected option, or elapsed time is not an answer or approval. Reuse an answer already given in the session instead of asking again.
- In a subagent/background run or explicit non-interactive mode (including `HANDOFF_MODE=1`), do not prompt the user directly. Use declared defaults only for optional preferences within the authorized scope and report assumptions. If a required decision, approval, or material scope/behavior choice remains unresolved, stop dependent work and return the missing decision and options to the parent/caller using its existing blocked/failure contract. Never invent consent or select a new scope to avoid blocking.

This delivery policy applies to this skill and its linked references. Preserve workflow-specific question scope, required confirmations, approval boundaries, and blocked-result rules.

## Shared project skill-context

Before mode routing or work, read existing files relative to the current project root in this order (reuse them if already loaded):

1. `.ai-factory/skill-context/global-skill-context.md` — all bundled skills.
2. `.ai-factory/skill-context/aif-commit/SKILL.md` — this skill.

Missing files are skipped; an existing unreadable file stops dependent work with its path.
Precedence: individual > build (when applicable) > global > skill defaults; retain non-conflicting instructions and check all outputs against the effective rules.
These layers customize workflow; they do not replace the project's rules/architecture hierarchy or relax explicit requirements, ownership, scope, safety/privacy, validation, or approval boundaries. Report conflicts with those boundaries instead of overriding them.
`global` is a project-local layer, not home-directory configuration. Custom/extension skills do not automatically use it.

Generate commit messages following the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) specification.

## Workflow

**FIRST:** Read `.ai-factory/config.yaml` if it exists to resolve:
- **Paths:** `paths.description`, `paths.architecture`, `paths.rules_file`, `paths.roadmap`, `paths.rules`, `paths.plan`, and `paths.plans`

If config.yaml doesn't exist, use defaults:

This file contains project-specific rules accumulated by `$aif-evolve` from patches,
codebase conventions, and tech-stack analysis. These rules are tailored to the current project.

**How to apply skill-context rules:**
- Treat them as **project-level overrides** for this skill's general instructions

  **the skill-context rule wins** (more specific context takes priority — same principle as nested CLAUDE.md files)
- When there is no conflict, apply both: general rules from SKILL.md + project rules from skill-context
- Do NOT ignore skill-context rules even if they seem to contradict this skill's defaults —
  they exist because the project's experience proved the default insufficient
- **CRITICAL:** skill-context rules apply to ALL outputs of this skill — including the commit
  message format and conventions. If a skill-context rule says "commits MUST follow format X"
  or "message MUST include Y" — you MUST comply. Generating a commit message that violates
  skill-context rules is a bug.

**Enforcement:** After generating any output artifact, verify it against all skill-context rules.
If any rule is violated — fix the output before presenting it to the user.

1. **Analyze Changes**
   - Run `git status` to see staged files
   - Run `git diff --cached` to see staged changes
   - In ordinary mode, if nothing is staged, show a warning and suggest staging
   - In task-bound mode, if nothing is staged, continue to map and selectively
     stage only the supplied group's proven changes as described below

2. **Resolve Active Plan Context (Read-Only, Optional)**
   - Resolve active plan using this read-only priority:
     1. `@<plan-file-or-directory>` argument, when the argument starts with `@`
     2. branch-based full plan or ultra bundle in `paths.plans`
     3. single full plan in `paths.plans`, or a single ultra bundle there
     4. fast plan at `paths.plan`
   - If the argument does not start with `@`, keep treating it as commit scope/context.
   - Legacy `@<plan-file>` syntax remains valid; the broader form additionally
     accepts an ultra directory or its `index.md`.
   - For branch-based full plan lookup:
     - get current branch with `git branch --show-current` when `git.enabled = true`
     - replace every `/` with `-` to get `<branch-stem>`
     - when `workflow.plan_id_format = sequential`, use `Glob` for both
       `paths.plans/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]_<branch-stem>.md` and
       `paths.plans/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]_<branch-stem>/index.md`
     - Read every directory candidate and retain it only when `index.md`
       contains exactly one `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`
     - use the highest-numbered valid artifact and emit `WARN [aif-commit]` when
       multiple valid candidates exist; if both shapes share the highest prefix,
       prefer ultra
     - if no valid sequential match exists, check
       `paths.plans/<branch-stem>/index.md` then
       `paths.plans/<branch-stem>.md`; Read the directory entrypoint before
       selection, ignore it unless it contains exactly one ultra marker, and
       warn and prefer ultra if both valid shapes exist
   - If git mode is off, branch lookup cannot resolve, or no branch-based plan
     exists, count root `*.md` full plans plus direct child `*/index.md`
     entrypoints containing `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; exclude the resolved fast-plan
     path and do not count phase files.
   - Before normalizing an explicit ultra directory or treating an explicit
     `index.md` as ultra, Read it and require exactly one
     `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; otherwise STOP with a plan-integrity error.
   - An automatically discovered directory entrypoint counts only when it
     contains `<!-- aif:plan-mode:ultra -->`; ignore unrelated `*/index.md` files.
   - If no active plan resolves, or the active plan has neither a classic `## Commit Plan` nor explicit task-based commit tasks, keep current staged-diff behavior unchanged.
   - If an active plan resolves, inspect it for both supported structures:
     - classic `## Commit Plan` section
     - task-based plan structure with explicit commit tasks such as `Commit changes with message "..."`
   - If neither format is found, keep current staged-diff behavior unchanged.
   - Never modify the active plan from this command.

3. **Use Commit Plan Grouping When Available**
   - If invoked by `$aif-implement` with an explicit task-bound commit request,
     treat the supplied plan path, commit task ID, dependency task IDs, exact
     message, and file/hunk map as the selected group. This mode takes
     precedence over ordinary grouping prompts: do not offer "Commit everything
     together" or expand the group to other plan tasks.
   - **Classic-group task-bound mode:** `$aif-implement` may invoke this mode
     for exactly one group from a classic `## Commit Plan`, using the explicit
     `classic-group` mode and supplying the exact resolved plan path, group
     number/name as written, complete task range, exact planned commit message,
     task IDs/descriptions and their `Files:`/hunk ownership evidence, plus the
     current `HANDOFF_MODE` value. This is task-bound mode, not ordinary
     plan-aware grouping. It does not require a commit-task ID or dependency
     list. Resolve the supplied path and verify the selected group exists in
     that plan; its group number/name, task range, and message must match the
     plan exactly. Reject missing, duplicate, ambiguous, or mismatched group
     metadata before changing the index. Re-read and map the exact task range
     from the plan; caller-supplied task/file evidence is a scope hint, not
     authority to expand the group. Never select adjacent groups or offer
     "Commit everything together."
   - Before changing the index, capture the complete outstanding change set
     against `HEAD` for the selected group, including staged, unstaged, and
     untracked changes. Use `git status --porcelain -uall` and
     `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to enumerate untracked paths;
     inspect each candidate's content and prove its ownership before staging.
     Map changes at hunk level when files overlap groups. This captured set is
     the completeness baseline for both task-based and classic-group
     task-bound execution.
   - Compare the selected group against both staged and unstaged changes.
     Commit only changes proven to belong to that group. Leave unrelated
     staged and unstaged changes untouched. Preserve unrelated staged and
     unstaged changes. Do not run `git add .`, unstage unrelated changes, or
     commit a pre-existing staged change outside the selected group.
   - If staged changes include unrelated work, the selected group overlaps
     other task work in a way that cannot be separated confidently, or any
     staged/unstaged hunk has unclear ownership, stop before changing the index
     and report the exact ambiguity. The caller must leave the plan commit task
     incomplete.
   - Stage every remaining proven change in the captured selected-group set,
     whether the index started empty or partially staged. Whole-file staging
     is allowed only for a disjoint group file with no unrelated unstaged
     edits; otherwise use hunk-level staging or stop. Explicitly stage
     selected, proven untracked files and verify they are no longer untracked.
     Before committing, verify that the staged diff contains the complete
